If you sell digital products, these are 3 legal documents you need to know about, and most sellers completely overlook number 3 👀 1️⃣ Digital Product Purchase Agreement This can establish the terms of the purchase, including restrictions on sharing or reselling your digital product and other important purchase terms. 2️⃣ Website/Store Terms & Conditions Your Terms & Conditions establish the rules for your online business and can address things like refunds, intellectual property, and limitations of liability. 3️⃣ Content Usage License If a brand or client pays to use your videos, templates, graphics, courses, or other content, a content usage license can clearly define how they can use it, where, for how long, and what happens if they go beyond those rights. Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. 💅🏾 And no, you don't necessarily need to spend hundreds on legal fees just to get foundational documents in place. Want to create and sell digital products? Here's what you actually do. 👇  1. Start with a problem. What problem are you solving for someone else? The best digital products make something easier, faster, or less overwhelming. 2. Create the solution. Turn what you know into something useful—a guide, checklist, planner, workbook, template, printable, mini-course, or resource. 3. Choose where to sell it. You can sell digital products through platforms like Etsy, Teachers Pay Teachers, Stan Store, or your own website. Choose the platform that makes sense for your product and audience. You can also publish them on Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing or Google Play.  4. Market it. Creating the product is only HALF the job. People have to find it! Use Pinterest, TikTok,  email, a blog, or search-friendly content to show people how your product solves their problem. 5. Learn from the first one...then create another. Your first product doesn't have to build financial freedom. It's your starting point. Create one useful product. Learn how to sell it. Improve. Then create another. Over time, you can build a collection of digital products that can be purchased while you're teaching, spending time with family, or simply living your life.  That's what I love about learning skills that can create income from home. I'm not looking for another job. I'm building more ways to earn—and more choices for my future. Financial freedom doesn't have to start with something huge. It can start with one product that solves one problem.
